title: Ohatsuki Ginkgo: Ancient Ohatsuki Ginkgos You Can Visit
meta_description: A ginkgo mutation that grows seeds on the leaf blade itself. Only seven trees in Japan carry the designation, three within two kilometres in Minobu.
intro: Most ginkgos hang their seeds on a stalk, apart from the branch. This mutation grows them straight out of the leaf blade itself, first described to Japanese science in July 1891 from a specimen in Minobu, Yamanashi. Only seven trees of the kind hold National Natural Monument status, and an unexplained three of them stand within two kilometres of each other in that one district: one toppled by Typhoon Trami in 2018 and still fruiting from its fallen trunk, another the sole male of the seven, its single fertile branch discovered only in 2011 after decades of nothing, and a third that local legend has the monk Nichiren planting himself in 1282. None has a documented planting date; all three ages here stay broad estimates rather than measurements.
